D1 research authoring, batch 87 (2026-09-27): two ASSOCIATION_ONLY draft mappings added at ranks 1-2 (anxiety-disorder, diplopia) pending qualified-human citation verification under docs/citation-verification-sop.md; mapping approval is not citation verification. Rank order is EVIDENCE-LED: the anxiety edge is first because two large pre-surgical cohorts report a prevalence and a third reports the treatment direction, while the diplopia edge is SECOND because its primary anchor STRATIFIES by diplopia status rather than measuring it as an outcome.

DIRECTION GUARD, APPLIED TO THE DIPLOPIA EDGE, AND IT IS THE FILE'S PRIMARY FINDING: the relationship is BIDIRECTIONAL and depends on strabismus type. In a paralytic or incomitant deviation the two images persist and diplopia is the presenting symptom; in an alternating or congenital deviation the brain suppresses the deviated image and diplopia is ABSENT. The edge is therefore registered as a GEOMETRIC COUPLING, not a consequence, and says so in its own association basis.

IATROGENIC-CAUSATION GUARD, APPLIED TO THE DIPLOPIA EDGE: one located anchor was designed specifically to measure POSTOPERATIVE DIPLOPIA in 79 adults who had NO DIPLOPIA IN ANY GAZE preoperatively. New diplopia in a patient with this identity may therefore be produced BY ITS TREATMENT, and a claim that attributes it to the underlying deviation would misattribute an iatrogenic event.

SHARED-EVIDENCE-SET DISCLOSURE: the two 220-patient anxiety anchors report the IDENTICAL 24 percent anxiety and 11 percent depression figures, share an institution and investigators, and the second names the first's instrument set. They are one evidence set, not two independent confirmations, and the anxiety and diplopia edges additionally share PMID 37558407.

SELF-SAME-EVIDENCE GUARD: all three anchors on both edges are SURGICAL POPULATIONS, selected on reaching an operating list, so no figure on this file may be read as a community prevalence. Strabismus is estimated to occur in 4 percent of the adult population, so a 24 percent anxiety figure among listed surgical patients cannot be extrapolated to that population.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Psychological distress is the most consistently documented accompaniment of this identity, and two independent surveys report the same figure while a third reports the direction of change under treatment. A cross-sectional study of 220 ADULT PATIENTS UNDERGOING STRABISMUS SURGERY at Moorfields Eye Hospital, mean age 45, with 58.6 PERCENT HAVING A CONCOMITANT DEVIATION, found that PRIOR TO SURGERY 24 PERCENT of participants were experiencing CLINICAL LEVELS OF ANXIETY and 11 PERCENT CLINICAL LEVELS OF DEPRESSION, stating that this is in line with other forms of facial disfigurement but HIGHER THAN OTHER CHRONIC DISEASES, and that QUALITY OF LIFE IMPROVED AND ANXIETY AND DEPRESSION WERE REDUCED after surgery, with approximately 6 PERCENT of the sample regretting surgery at either 3 or 6 months (PMID 27651232). A cross-sectional study of 220 adult patients with strabismus due to undergo realignment surgery, assessed with the HOSPITAL ANXIETY AND DEPRESSION SCALE and the AS-20, independently found THE SAME 11 PERCENT at clinical levels of depression and 24 PERCENT at clinical anxiety, and reported that although mood and quality of life were associated with age and diplopia, IT WAS BELIEFS AND COGNITIONS WHICH WERE MORE CONSISTENTLY ASSOCIATED WITH WELL-BEING, including feelings of social anxiety and avoidance, a belief that strabismus has negative consequences, poor understanding of strabismus, social support, fear of negative evaluation and the perceived visibility of the condition (PMID 24390164). A study of 59 patients assessed preoperatively and approximately 3 months after strabismus surgery with strabismus-specific psychosocial instruments and the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale found that POSTOPERATIVE STRABISMUS-RELATED QUALITY OF LIFE WAS HIGHER AFTER SURGERY AND ANXIETY AND DEPRESSION LEVELS WERE LOWER, and that SATISFACTION WITH SURGERY WAS LOWER WITH A HIGHER POSTOPERATIVE ANGLE AND DIPLOPIA (PMID 37558407). Recorded as documented association only, with the modifier identified by one anchor carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and THE TWO 220-PATIENT SURVEYS ARE NOT INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION. They report the identical 24 percent anxiety and 11 percent depression figures, they draw on the same institution and the same investigators, and the second names the first's instrument set, so this is ONE EVIDENCE SET rather than two, and it is recorded as such. Both are also SELECTED ON PENDING SURGERY, so their figures describe people who have already reached an operating list and cannot be read as a community prevalence, which will under-represent people with strabismus who never seek surgery and will over-represent those whose symptoms are severe enough to warrant it. A FINDING THAT CUTS AGAINST A SIMPLE CAUSAL READING IS CARRIED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: the second anchor reports that although mood was associated with age and diplopia, IT WAS BELIEFS AND COGNITIONS WHICH WERE MORE CONSISTENTLY ASSOCIATED WITH WELL-BEING, naming social anxiety and avoidance, a belief that strabismus has negative consequences, poor understanding of the condition, social support, fear of negative evaluation and perceived visibility, and the same anchor's authors state that LONGITUDINAL STUDIES ARE NEEDED TO EXPLORE THE DIRECTION OF CAUSALITY. A further finding is carried because it is clinically uncomfortable: the first anchor reports that anxiety and depression REDUCED after surgery and that 6 PERCENT REGRETTED HAVING UNDERGONE IT, so the condition's most plausible remedy carries its own psychological cost and the edge may not be used to argue that surgical correction resolves distress. Individual claims require a dated ophthalmic diagnosis with the STRABISMUS TYPE, the deviation angle measured in prism diopters, the duration of the deviation, whether it is intermittent or constant, and whether binocular vision is present documented, a structured anxiety instrument administered and scored with the instrument and its threshold named, a belief-and-attitude assessment where the cognitive pathway is at issue, a documented surgical and non-surgical treatment history, and a clinical determination separating an anxiety disorder from social anxiety about appearance, from fear of negative evaluation, from a pre-existing anxiety disorder and from distress attributable to any concurrent condition.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is an evaluative threat sustained by a visible and uncontrollable sign: strabismus is visible to others, the deviation is intermittent or unpredictable in many types, so the sufferer cannot predict when the eye will turn, and each unpredictable occurrence in a social or evaluative setting is a discrete social-evaluative threat; repeated such threats produce anticipatory vigilance and avoidance, the avoidance reduces the corrective social experience that would test the belief that others react badly, and the belief therefore goes untested and strengthens, which is the located finding that beliefs and cognitions rather than clinical variables were the more consistent correlates of well-being.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at two-independent-authored-but-related-preoperative-surgery-cohorts and a pre-post-surgery-psychometric-cohort class, following the file's existing ophthalmic and psychological pathway scope. The Moorfields cohort is the anchor that supplies the prevalence, 24 percent clinical anxiety and 11 percent clinical depression before surgery, the explicit comparison with other forms of facial disfigurement and with other chronic diseases, the finding that quality of life improved and anxiety and depression reduced after surgery, and the 6 percent regret rate, all four of which are registered together because registering the improvement without the regret rate would misrepresent the intervention (PMID 27651232). The second 220-patient cohort is registered for the belief-and-cognition finding, which is what makes the mechanism claim evaluative rather than somatic and which the located evidence identifies as more consistently associated with well-being than age or diplopia, together with its authors' own statement that longitudinal studies are needed to explore the direction of causality (PMID 24390164). The 59-patient pre-post cohort is registered for the treatment-effect direction, anxiety and depression lower after surgery and satisfaction lower with a larger postoperative angle and with diplopia, which are the located findings that make this edge modifiable and that constrain how it may be used (PMID 37558407). Because the two large surveys are not independent, because all three are surgical populations, and because the located evidence cannot order the condition and the beliefs, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only and states no community prevalence.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The relationship between this identity and diplopia is the one place in the located literature where the direction of the edge cannot be fixed, and that ambiguity is the located finding. A systematic review examining the impact of strabismus on quality of life in adults WITH AND WITHOUT DIPLOPIA reports that QUALITY OF LIFE DIFFERS FOR STRABISMUS PATIENTS BASED ON THEIR DIPLOPIA STATUS, that PATIENTS WITH DIPLOPIA TEND TO HAVE MORE CONCERNS RELATING TO FUNCTIONAL quality of life whereas PATIENTS WITHOUT DIPLOPIA HAVE PRIMARILY PSYCHOSOCIAL CONCERNS, and that two diplopia-specific quality-of-life questionnaires have been designed to assess quality of life and the perceived severity of symptoms (PMID 24359806). The same review notes that strabismus has been estimated to occur in 4 PERCENT of the adult population (PMID 24359806). A prospective study of 79 ADULTS WITH NO DIPLOPIA IN ANY GAZE who had childhood-onset strabismus and were scheduled for strabismus surgery, assessed with a standardised diplopia questionnaire in 7 gaze positions and the Adult Strabismus-20, was designed to DESCRIBE THE FREQUENCY OF POSTOPERATIVE DIPLOPIA, which is a finding that the condition and the intervention can BOTH PRODUCE the target, and in which diplopia was also a determinant of lower postoperative quality of life (PMID 31586582). A 59-patient study found that satisfaction with strabismus surgery was LOWER WITH A HIGHER POSTOPERATIVE ANGLE AND DIPLOPIA, and that diplopia was a determinant of lower postoperative quality of life (PMID 37558407). Recorded as documented association only, with the direction ambiguity carried openly rather than resolved in the edge's own name.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and THE EDGE IS AMBIDIRECTIONAL, which is stated in the association basis rather than concealed: whether diplopia precedes or follows a strabismus depends on which type it is. In a PARALYTIC OR INCOMMITANT deviation the misalignment arises from a weak or restricted muscle, so the two images remain and DIPLOPIA IS THE PRESENTING SYMPTOM, running diplopia to strabismus; in an ALTERNATING OR CONGENITAL deviation the brain suppresses the deviated image during childhood, so binocular vision is lost and DIPLOPIA IS ABSENT, running strabismus to the absence of diplopia. No located anchor separates these two populations, and the systematic review instead treats diplopia status as a STRATIFIER OF THE STRABISMUS POPULATION rather than an outcome, which is the located reason the relationship is registered as a coupling rather than a consequence. A SECOND FINDING MAKES THE AMBIGUITY OPERATIONALLY IMPORTANT RATHER THAN MERELY THEORETICAL: the prospective study was designed to measure POSTOPERATIVE DIPLOPIA IN ADULTS WHO HAD NONE PREOPERATIVELY, so in this identity the target can be PRODUCED BY THE TREATMENT as well as the condition, and a claim that attributes new diplopia to the underlying deviation rather than to the surgery would misattribute an iatrogenic event. The 79-patient study reports the frequency of that postoperative diplopia in a deliberately diplopia-free population, which is the located evidence that it is a real and measurable outcome of intervention. Individual claims require a dated ophthalmic diagnosis with the STRABISMUS TYPE documented, since a paralytic and an alternating deviation have opposite relationships to diplopia, the deviation angle in prism diopters, the presence or absence of binocular vision and of a suppression scotoma, whether the deviation is congenital or acquired and the age of onset, a gaze-by-gaze diplopia assessment with the testing positions named, a documented surgical and non-surgical treatment history, and a clinical determination separating diplopia from this identity's deviation from that of a cranial nerve palsy, from a decompensated phoria and from a decompensated convergence insufficiency.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is the geometry of fixation and binocular correspondence: when the two eyes fix on different targets, the images fall on non-corresponding retinal points and the brain cannot fuse them, so a single visual percept is impossible and either two images are perceived, producing diplopia, or the deviated image is suppressed, producing single vision at the cost of binocular depth; the vector is therefore the misalignment geometry itself, and the located evidence registers both possible outputs of the same geometry, which is why the mechanism claim names the geometry rather than either symptom.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at systematic-review, prospective-pre-post-intervention-cohort and pre-post-psychometric-cohort class, following the file's existing ophthalmic and neurological pathway scope. The systematic review is the anchor that carries the edge because it is the located source that stratifies this population BY DIPLOPIA STATUS rather than treating diplopia as an outcome, and it is therefore the evidence that the relationship is a coupling rather than a consequence; its finding that patients with diplopia report functional concerns while those without report psychosocial concerns is also what makes the target clinically consequential in the differing way the review describes (PMID 24359806). The prospective 79-patient study is registered because it is the located evidence that this target can be PRODUCED BY THE TREATMENT of this identity, having been designed specifically to measure postoperative diplopia in adults who had none in any gaze preoperatively, and a claim that attributed such an event to the underlying deviation would misattribute an iatrogenic outcome (PMID 31586582). The 59-patient study is registered for the independent finding that diplopia was a determinant of lower postoperative quality of life, which corroborates clinical significance without addressing direction (PMID 37558407). Because the located evidence stratifies by diplopia rather than following it, and because one located anchor shows the target arising from the intervention, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only and records the bidirectionality on the face of the edge.

A decompensated phoria or convergence insufficiency presenting as intermittent diplopia without a childhood-onset deviation, which is a different mechanism from either the paralytic or the alternating case

sourceReferences.citation: McBain HB, Au CK, Hancox J, et al. The impact of strabismus on quality of life in adults with and without diplopia: a systematic review. Surv Ophthalmol. 2014 Mar-Apr;59(2):185-91. doi: 10.1016/j.survophthal.2013.04.001. PMID 24359806.
sourceReferences.note: SYSTEMATIC REVIEW examining the impact of strabismus on quality of life in ADULTS BOTH WITH AND WITHOUT DIPLOPIA, focusing primarily on quality of life, and highlighting the value of measuring it, the ways in which it can be measured, and the impact of the disease, of diplopia and of surgery on the patient. THE KEY FINDING IS THAT QUALITY OF LIFE DIFFERS FOR STRABISMUS PATIENTS BASED ON THEIR DIPLOPIA STATUS: PATIENTS WITH DIPLOPIA TEND TO HAVE MORE CONCERNS RELATING TO FUNCTIONAL quality of life, whereas PATIENTS WITHOUT DIPLOPIA HAVE PRIMARILY PSYCHOSOCIAL CONCERNS. The authors note that two diplopia-specific questionnaires have been designed to assess quality of life and the perceived severity of symptoms, and that further research is needed to identify the variables which influence quality of life so that appropriate support can be given to all patients. The review also records that strabismus has been estimated to occur in 4 PERCENT of the adult population. Registered as the anchor that STRATIFIES this population by diplopia status rather than treating diplopia as an outcome, which is the located reason the edge is registered as a coupling rather than a consequence. sourceReferences.citation: Wang JY, Leske DA, Hatt SR, et al. Diplopia after strabismus surgery for adults with nondiplopic childhood-onset strabismus. J AAPOS. 2019 Dec;23(6):313.e1-313.e5. doi: 10.1016/j.jaapos.2019.07.005. PMID 31586582.
sourceReferences.note: PROSPECTIVE STUDY OF 79 ADULTS WITH NO DIPLOPIA IN ANY GAZE who had CHILDHOOD-ONSET STRABISMUS and were scheduled for strabismus surgery, designed to DESCRIBE THE FREQUENCY OF POSTOPERATIVE DIPLOPIA and to report health-related quality-of-life outcomes. Diplopia was assessed preoperatively and at 6 weeks and 1 year postoperatively using A STANDARDISED DIPLOPIA QUESTIONNAIRE WITH 5 RESPONSE OPTIONS IN 7 GAZE POSITIONS, and health-related quality of life was assessed with the Adult Strabismus-20, which has self-perception, interactions, reading function and general function domains. Registered for the specific and important reason that it measures this target ARISING FROM THE TREATMENT of this identity in a population that had none beforehand, so a claim attributing such diplopia to the underlying deviation would MISATTRIBUTE AN IATROGENIC OUTCOME. DISCLOSED: an uncontrolled single-arm study in a deliberately diplopia-free population, so it reports postoperative frequency and not a complication rate for untreated disease.

Implementing strabismus-specific psychosocial questionnaires in everyday clinical practice: mental health and quality of life in the context of strabismus surgery. BMJ Open Ophthalmol. 2023 Aug;8(1). doi: 10.1136/bmjophth-2023-001334. PMID 37558407.
sourceReferences.note: STUDY OF 59 PATIENTS assessed preoperatively and approximately 3 months after strabismus surgery using strabismus-specific psychosocial instruments and the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale. SATISFACTION WITH SURGERY WAS LOWER WITH A HIGHER POSTOPERATIVE ANGLE AND WITH DIPLOPIA, and DIPLOPIA WAS ALSO A DETERMINANT OF LOWER POSTOPERATIVE QUALITY OF LIFE. Postoperative quality of life was higher after surgery and anxiety and depression levels were lower. Registered for the independent finding that this target determines postoperative satisfaction and quality of life. DISCLOSED: it corroborates CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE WITHOUT ADDRESSING DIRECTION, since it measures diplopia after the intervention and does not compare against an untreated deviation, and it has 59 patients with a 3-month postoperative assessment and no control group.

governanceNotes: IDENTITY SCREEN, batch 87: no alias duplication found. The catalog carries diplopia, nystagmus, ptosis, strabismus and related ophthalmic identities separately; diplopia is a SYMPTOM and strabismus is a MOTILITY FINDING, and both are registered as distinct identities with no alias overlap. The relationship between them is therefore not a duplication and is registered as a coupling with its direction disclosed.

INCOMING-EDGE MAP, batch 87: this identity had ZERO registered incoming edges and ZERO registered outgoing edges before this batch, so both edges are new. Targets anxiety-disorder at 27 and diplopia at 1, with the latter being among the most thinly covered ophthalmic targets in the registry.

A MISSING IDENTITY WITHHELD, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT REFUSAL IN THIS FILE: amblyopia has NO IDENTITY IN THE CATALOG, and amblyopia is the single most consequential consequence of this identity, being the visual-deficiency outcome that a unilateral or alternating deviation produces through suppression during the critical period. An edge could not be written because the target does not exist, so the gap is recorded here in the todo list and in these notes so that it is visible to whoever next curates the condition catalog, rather than being silently absorbed into the diplopia edge which is a different thing entirely.

TWO ANCHORS NOT INDEPENDENT: the two 220-patient anxiety cohorts report identical figures, share an institution and investigators and use the same instruments, and the two edges additionally share a 59-patient anchor. Recorded so that the file's three anchors are never counted as more than one-and-a-half independent lines of evidence.

A REGRET FINDING CARRIED RATHER THAN OMITTED: the 220-patient surgical cohort reports that anxiety and depression reduced after surgery and that approximately 6 percent regretted having undergone it, registered on the anxiety edge so the intervention is not presented as unambiguously psychologically beneficial.
